skill.name: azure-compliance
skill.description: Audit Azure compliance with Azure Quick Review, azqr, and Key Vault expiration checks. It helps review resource posture, policy findings, and remediation guidance.
skill.summary: Assess Azure compliance, security posture, and Key Vault expiration risk.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly documentation false positives from Markdown examples, SDK snippets, placeholders, and Azure tool names. I found no prompt injection text, but the Key Vault workflow can invoke secret retrieval commands that may expose values if outputs are not redacted. Treat the skill as requiring confirmation for Azure access, CLI fallback, and any remediation action.

remediation.issue: Key Vault secret retrieval can expose secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Use metadata-only APIs for expiration checks. Redact values and request explicit user approval before any secret get operation.

remediation.issue: Azure CLI fallback uses local credentials outside MCP controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before CLI fallback. Show the exact command, vault, subscription, and tenant before execution.

remediation.issue: Remediation templates include mutable Azure commands.
remediation.suggestion: Keep remediation in report-only mode by default. Require change approval before applying Azure CLI, Bicep, or PowerShell fixes.

content.user_title: Audit Azure Compliance and Key Vault Expiration
content.value_statement: Azure teams need clear evidence for compliance, security posture, and expiring Key Vault items. This skill guides azqr scans, resource review, and prioritized remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides Azure Quick Review scans for subscription, resource group, management group, or service scopes.
Interprets azqr workbook sheets for recommendations, impacted resources, inventory, Advisor, Defender, and Policy.
Audits Key Vault keys, secrets, and certificates for expiration status and missing expiration dates.
Maps findings to security, reliability, cost, operations, and governance categories.
Provides remediation options using Azure Portal, Azure CLI, Bicep, or follow-up scans.
limitations: Requires Azure authentication and permissions for the selected subscription, resource group, or Key Vault.
Does not replace formal compliance certification or legal review.
May expose sensitive metadata if scan outputs are shared without review.
Remediation commands should be reviewed before use in production.

use_cases.title: Run a subscription compliance scan
use_cases.description: Assess an Azure subscription with azqr and summarize critical security, reliability, and governance findings.

use_cases.title: Track Key Vault expiration risk
use_cases.description: Find expired or soon-expiring keys, secrets, and certificates before outages occur.

use_cases.title: Prepare remediation planning
use_cases.description: Convert scan findings into prioritized tasks with effort, impact, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check Key Vault expirations
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit Key Vault <vault-name> for expired items and items expiring within 30 days. Summarize counts, risks, and next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Run a resource group scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an azqr assessment for resource group <resource-group> in subscription <subscription-id>. Focus on security and reliability findings.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these azqr findings and rank the top remediation actions by severity, impact, effort, and validation method.

prompt_templates.title: Compare scan results over time
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the latest azqr scan with the previous report. Identify closed findings, new findings, and repeated issues by owner.

output_examples.input: Audit Key Vault expiration for a production vault with a 30-day threshold.
output: Summary: 42 items reviewed across keys, secrets, and certificates.
Critical: 2 expired secrets require immediate rotation.
Recommended action: set expiration policies and assign owners for rotation.

output_examples.input: Analyze an azqr workbook for subscription security posture.
output: Top finding: public endpoints remain enabled on storage and SQL resources.
Priority: address critical exposure before reliability and cost items.
Validation: rerun the assessment after changes and compare impacted resource counts.

output_examples.input: Prepare a remediation plan for Defender and Policy findings.
output_examples.output: The plan groups findings by severity, assigns owners, lists approval needs, and separates reporting from remediation execution.

best_practices: Confirm scope and permissions before running scans or Key Vault checks.
Review outputs for secrets, identifiers, and cost data before sharing.
Use report-only mode first, then apply remediation through approved change processes.
anti_patterns: Running broad scans without confirming subscription or resource group scope.
Pasting secret values or raw Key Vault outputs into shared tickets.
Applying remediation commands to production without review and rollback planning.

faq.question: Does this skill require Azure access?
faq.answer: Yes. The user must authenticate to Azure and have read permissions for the selected resources.

faq.question: Can it run azqr scans?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides workflow guidance and uses the Azure MCP azqr tool when available.

faq.question: Does it retrieve Key Vault secret values?
faq.answer: It should focus on metadata such as expiration dates. Users should avoid sharing secret values and redact outputs.

faq.question: Can it fix compliance findings automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides remediation guidance. Production changes should follow approval and change management.

faq.question: What outputs can it analyze?
faq.answer: It can summarize azqr workbook sheets, Key Vault expiration results, and Azure Resource Graph query results.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for compliance certification?
faq.answer: No. It supports internal assessment and planning, but formal audits need approved controls and reviewers.
